shortDescription.text: Paths differ only by case

help.text: Two paths that differ only by case are one file on Windows and default macOS; a checkout keeps one and silently loses the other. Fix: Rename one; keep one spelling.

shortDescription.text: Name longer than 255 UTF-8 bytes (cannot exist on Linux)

help.text: Linux file systems limit a name to 255 bytes (NAME_MAX), but NTFS counts UTF-16 units: a short-looking name of CJK/emoji characters can be too long on Linux. macOS/APFS limit not verified here. Fix: Shorten the name.

shortDescription.text: Path component longer than 255 UTF-16 units

help.text: NTFS allows 255 UTF-16 units per name. Fix: Shorten the name.

shortDescription.text: Sibling names that look alike (homoglyphs, ligatures, full-width)

help.text: Two different files whose names look alike (Cyrillic/Greek letters, ligatures, full-width forms): a reviewer cannot tell README.md from RЕADME.md. Uses a small curated subset of Unicode confusables.txt, so it is not exhaustive. Fix: Rename one; ASCII is safest.

shortDescription.text: Git path has a '.' or empty component

help.text: A git tree can hold an entry named '.' or an empty name (git fsck: hasDot, emptyName); Git refuses to check it out. Fix: Remove the entry from the tree.

shortDescription.text: Path has a '..' component (walks out of its folder)

help.text: A git tree can hold an entry named '..'; checking it out would write outside the folder. Git refuses it (git fsck: hasDotdot). Fix: Remove the entry from the tree.

shortDescription.text: Path component is, or aliases, the .git directory

help.text: On Windows/macOS this name resolves to the repository's own .git; a checkout through it can overwrite hooks and run code (CVE-2014-9390 family). Fix: Delete or rename it by hand; never `git mv` it to `.git`.

shortDescription.text: Alias of .gitmodules/.gitattributes/.gitignore/.mailmap

help.text: A non-canonical spelling of .gitmodules/.gitattributes/.gitignore/.mailmap that Git reads as the real file on case- or alias-insensitive filesystems. Fix: Delete it, or rename to the canonical name if intended.

shortDescription.text: Character Windows rejects in file names

help.text: < > : " | ? * \ and control characters are rejected in Windows names. Fix: Replace the character; `--format gitmv` proposes a name.

shortDescription.text: Path is not valid UTF-8

help.text: The name is not valid UTF-8, so Git for Windows cannot reproduce it. Fix: Rename it with valid UTF-8 (git mv with the escaped bytes shown).

shortDescription.text: Invisible or bidi format character in name

help.text: Bidi or zero-width characters make a name display as something else (Trojan Source). Fix: Remove the character.

shortDescription.text: One word mixes Latin with Cyrillic/Greek look-alikes

help.text: A single word mixes Latin with Cyrillic/Greek look-alike letters (pаypal). Fix: Use one script per word.

shortDescription.text: Name is not NFC-normalized

help.text: A decomposed name may be treated as a different file by macOS and Linux tools. Fix: Rename to the composed (NFC) form.

shortDescription.text: Operating-system metadata file (.DS_Store, Thumbs.db, ._*)

help.text: Finder/Explorer metadata committed by accident. Fix: git rm it and add it to .gitignore.

shortDescription.text: Path exceeds Windows MAX_PATH when cloned

help.text: Over MAX_PATH once cloned under a typical Windows folder; fails unless long paths are enabled (Git: core.longpaths). Fix: Shorten folder names or tune --prefix-len.

shortDescription.text: Path beyond macOS (1024) or Linux (4096) PATH_MAX

help.text: macOS's PATH_MAX is 1024 and Linux's 4096 bytes (including the NUL); a relative path alone beyond that cannot be created. 4096+ bytes is an error and is kept out of the collision checks. macOS value from sys/syslimits.h, not run on macOS here. Fix: Flatten the folder tree.

shortDescription.text: Windows reserved device name (CON, NUL, COM1, ...)

help.text: Windows treats CON, PRN, AUX, NUL, COM1-9, LPT1-9 (and a few more) as devices, with any extension: the file cannot be created or opened. Fix: Rename it (CON.txt -> con_notes.txt).

shortDescription.text: Name equals the 8.3 short name of a sibling

help.text: NTFS gives long names a hidden 8.3 alias; a tracked file named like that alias clashes with it. Fix: Rename the tilde-style file.

shortDescription.text: .gitmodules that is too large or does not parse

help.text: .gitmodules over 1 MiB (Git's fsck refuses it) or a line Git cannot parse. Fix: Repair the file.

shortDescription.text: .gitmodules submodule name with '..' (CVE-2018-11235)

help.text: git builds .git/modules/<name> from the name; '..' writes outside .git/modules and can plant a hook (CVE-2018-11235). Git's own fsck rejects it (gitmodulesName). Fix: Delete the .gitmodules entry.

shortDescription.text: .gitmodules path starting with '-'

help.text: A path starting with '-' can be read as an option. Fix: Use a normal path.

shortDescription.text: .gitmodules update setting that is a '!' command

help.text: update = !command would run a command taken from .gitmodules; Git's fsck rejects it (gitmodulesUpdate). Fix: Remove the setting.

shortDescription.text: .gitmodules url that Git or ssh reads as an option or command

help.text: A url starting with '-' is read as an option (CVE-2017-1000117); an encoded newline can inject into credential helpers (CVE-2020-11008); ext:: runs a command (disabled by default). Fix: Use a normal https:// or ssh:// url.

shortDescription.text: Tracked symlink (needs privileges on Windows)

help.text: On Windows a symlink needs Developer Mode/admin plus core.symlinks=true; otherwise Git writes a small text file. Fix: Avoid symlinks, or `--disable symlink` if the repo needs them.

shortDescription.text: Symlink target contains a backslash

help.text: A backslash is a separator on Windows and an ordinary character elsewhere. Fix: Use forward slashes in link targets.

shortDescription.text: Symlink points outside the repository

help.text: The link points outside the repository or is absolute. Fix: Use a relative in-repo target.

shortDescription.text: Symlink named like Git metadata

help.text: A symlink named .gitmodules (etc.) redirects what Git reads and writes. Fix: Remove the link.

shortDescription.text: Path below a tracked symlink

help.text: A path below a tracked symlink can be written through the link to anywhere (CVE-2018-11235 style). Fix: Remove the link or the path below it.

shortDescription.text: Name ends with a dot

help.text: Windows silently drops trailing dots. Fix: Remove the trailing dot.

shortDescription.text: Name ends with a space

help.text: Windows silently drops trailing spaces, so the file 'disappears' or collides. Fix: Remove the trailing space.

shortDescription.text: Paths differ only by Unicode normalization

help.text: NFC and NFD spellings look identical; macOS treats them as one name. Fix: Rename to the NFC spelling and delete the duplicate.

message.text: paths differ only by case and cannot coexist on Windows: src/Util.py, src/util.py
'.GITMODULES' is a non-canonical spelling/alias of .gitmodules: on a case- or alias-insensitive filesystem Git reads it as the real file
'CON.md' collides with the Windows device name CON
'trail.' ends with a dot — Windows silently strips it
paths differ only by Unicode normalization and are the same file on macOS: 'cafe\u0301.txt', 'caf\u00e9.txt'
'a\u202eb.txt' contains invisible/bidi format character(s) U+202E — the name can display differently from what it is
'cafe\u0301.txt' is not NFC-normalized (composed form: 'caf\xe9.txt'); macOS and Linux tools can treat the two as different files
